body:
_Migrated from issue #1389, filed 2026-08-05._

The next-pick ranker demotes an issue to the bottom bucket once a fix for it has shipped, and nothing lets a reporter's "it still doesn't work" pull it back up. Shipping is treated as evidence of doneness, which is exactly the state in which a pushback is most likely and most important.

`scripts/rank-next-pick.sh:124`:

```
| . + {bucket: (if .handled then 5 elif .owe_reply then -1 else 0 end)}
```

`handled` wins over everything else, and there is no `pushback` term anywhere in the script.

`scripts/autopilot-tick.sh:676` says the opposite:

> label `pushback` on a regression so the rank booster surfaces it

There is no such booster. The label is written by `verification-sweep.sh:352` and read by nothing that affects priority — `gen-followup-board.sh` lists it in `STATE_LABELS`, and that is the end of it.

**Live instance: #324.** It is the highest-reach ticket in the repo (5 reactions, 3 commenters, `reach_score: 8`; almost everything else is 0), it is 71 days old, it is on the web-reader sync program, and on 2026-08-04 @jrodrigoferreira posted a detailed reproduction against v4.1.29 showing the shipped half does not work for them — the reader opens at 0% instead of the Kobo position, a web-side move to 80% never reaches the device, and a Kobo sync then rolls the displayed percentage back to 70% while the actual resume position stays at 80%.

Its record in `state/next-pick.json` this tick:

```json
{ "number": 324, "reach_score": 8, "handled": true, "owe_reply": false, "bucket": 5 }
```

Bottom bucket. It also does not appear on the follow-up board, because `owe_reply` requires the last comment to be more than two days old and this one was six hours old at rank time. So for the 48 hours in which a fresh regression report is most actionable, it is visible in neither the pick queue nor the board.

Three separate mechanisms have to line up for this to happen, which is why it is worth fixing at the ranker rather than patching a symptom:

1. `handled: true` demotes it, *because* v4.1.29 shipped half the feature.
2. `owe_reply: false` hides it from the board, because the report is fresh.
3. `verification-sweep.sh:351` only acts when `"pushback" not in cand["labels"]`, so once the label is applied the sweep is permanently silent on that thread. Correct as an idempotency guard, but it means the label is a terminal state rather than a queue.

Suggested fix, smallest first:

- Give `pushback` a bucket ahead of fresh work, e.g. `if .has_pushback then -2 elif .handled then 5 …`, so a regression outranks new feature work rather than being buried under it. This is the one that matters; the others are cleanup.
- Either implement the booster `autopilot-tick.sh:676` describes or delete that line. A comment describing a mechanism that does not exist is worse than no comment — it reads as coverage.
- Consider whether `handled` should be cleared when a non-`new-usemame` comment arrives after the shipping comment. "We shipped something" and "the user's problem is solved" are different claims, and the ranker currently conflates them.

Worth noting the general shape, since it has now bitten twice (see #1388): every one of these sweeps is scoped by a label, and the thread that most needs attention is routinely the one whose label just changed. A label is a queue only if something drains it.
title: Ranker buries a shipped-then-broken issue: 'handled' outranks everything and 'pushback' is read by nothing (#324 is bucket 5)
